title: Add KMS credential rotation helper and RBAC drift detector
author: Aisha Raman
description:
Motivation: customers and internal audits highlighted two recurring operational gaps: (1) stale/overprivileged RBAC bindings drifting from policy intent over time, and (2) long-lived KMS credentials without a safe automated rotation path. This PR introduces two complementary components: an off-path KMS credential rotation helper (agentless rotation orchestration + audit-safe key metadata updates) and an RBAC drift detector that emits structured audit events and can optionally auto-quarantine suspect bindings.

Summary of changes (high level): added a small rotation orchestrator service under pkg/kms/rotation, a safe API surface for rotating wrapped keys without re-encrypting active tokens, added an rbac drift detector binary under tools/rbac-drift-detector with a scheduled runner and a policy-to-state comparator, wired drift detector to the audit pipeline so drift events are forwarded to the compliance topic, and updated the console telemetry to display last-rotation timestamps and drift scores per-tenant.

Checklist: 
- [x] Core rotation orchestration implementation
- [x] RBAC drift comparator and scoring heuristic (pluggable)
- [x] Structured audit events for rotation and drift with immutable metadata (tenant, region_pin, key_origin)
- [x] Unit and integration tests for happy and edge cases (rotation failure, partial apply, retry loop)
- [x] Migration for persisted rotation metadata (no data movement for keys)
- [x] Docs and quickstart examples for Private customers to enable rotation agent and configure drift thresholds

Security considerations: rotation helper only accepts requests signed by operator service principals with the new temporary-operator scope; RBAC drift detector runs read-only by default and only proposes quarantines (requires explicit enablement via operator flag). All rotation operations emit an immutable audit event that includes CMK region_pin and origin to satisfy residency controls.

Testing & rollout: tested on staging (eu-west-1) against a synthetic tenant fleet; performed canary rollout to 5% of tenant fleet with automatic rollback on increased error budget. The drift detector initially runs in audit-only mode for 2 weeks to collect baseline scores before any quarantine actions can be enabled.

Notes: this PR intentionally avoids touching token issuance code path to minimize blast radius; rotation works by adding a rotated_key metadata pointer and performing background rewraps for long-lived artifacts.

review_threads:
Ethan Cole: Can the rotation flow guarantee zero downtime for in-flight requests? Please clarify the rewrap cadence and backoff strategy.
Aisha Raman: Rewrap happens async; orchestrator provides a transient compatibility pointer (rotated_key_alias) and we keep previous key active until all in-flight tokens are reissued or TTL expiry. Added paragraph in orchestrator.go and tests to simulate heavy in-flight traffic.

Mariana Velasquez: The drift comparator uses heuristic X which may flag service accounts with ephemeral privileges as drift — can we add a whitelist?
Aisha Raman: Added pluggable whitelist file and tenant-scoped exceptions; drift detector defaults to audit-only mode so no live quarantines until whitelists reviewed.

Devon Huang: CI flakiness observed on rotation e2e. The integration matrix fails intermittently when KMS emulate returns 429.
Aisha Raman: Added retry with jitter and bumped the fake KMS throughput in the test harness; CI pipeline now retries failing matrix jobs once.
release_notes: Added a KMS credential rotation orchestrator (agentless rewrap + safe metadata promotion) and an RBAC drift detector that emits structured compliance events. Both features are opt-in and controlled via feature flags; rollout in audit-only mode by default.
